page: Vultr vx1-m-48c-384g-2880s is a memory-optimized server belonging to the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 24 physical AMD EPYC cores running at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system is equipped with 384.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage is bundled with 2880 GB of NVMe SSD capacity, and there are no GPUs present. The CPU supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, AVX-512 BF16, and SHA extensions.

Benchmark results highlight top-tier single-core and multi-core performance. In Geekbench testing, both single-core and multi-core scores rank in the top 10%, alongside top-tier results in image and text processing. Memory bandwidth for large-block read and write operations also places in the top 10%, demonstrating efficient data throughput. Multi-core stress-ng tests, Passmark CPU scores, and Redis SET operations register in the top 25%, indicating strong capabilities under heavy concurrent workloads.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this instance offers a dense allocation of dedicated AMD EPYC resources and high-capacity NVMe storage, making it a viable option for memory-intensive workloads without the overhead of specialized GPU hardware. The combination of 384.0 GB of RAM, fast local storage, and strong multi-threaded performance makes this server well-suited for large-scale databases, memory-cached web serving, software compilation, and medium-scale LLM inference tasks.
